plain_english: In truth it is not that ninefold self, not the heap of words, not Bhairava; not that three-headed god either, nor the nature of the three powers.
sanskrit_cite: tattvato na navātmāsau śabdarāśir na bhairavaḥ | na cāsau triśirā devo na ca śaktitrayātmakaḥ

plain_english: Not made of nāda's drop, either; not the checkers of the moon; not joined to the wheel's course, not the power-formed.
sanskrit_cite: nādabindumayo vāpi na candrārdhanirodhikāḥ | na cakrakramasambhinno na ca śaktisvarūpakaḥ

plain_english: These terrors of unawakened minds are strong indeed; like a mother's sweet, all of it is declared for the sake of going on.
sanskrit_cite: aprabuddhamatīnāṃ hi etā balavibhīṣikāḥ | mātṛmodakavat sarvaṃ pravṛttyarthaṃ udāhṛtam

plain_english: Free of direction, time and counting — with no particular place or point: it cannot be pointed out; untellable in the end.
sanskrit_cite: dikkālakalanonmuktā deśoddeśāviśeṣinī | vyapadeṣṭum aśakyāsāv akathyā paramārthataḥ

plain_english: Joy of inner self-taste, unhoused in fancy's range — that full-formed state, Bhairavī, of Bhairava's own self.
sanskrit_cite: antaḥsvānubhavānandā vikalponmuktagocarā | yāvasthā bharitākārā bhairavī bhairavātmanaḥ

plain_english: That body must be known in truth: stainless, filling the world — in such a supreme reality, who is worshipped, and which one is pleased?
sanskrit_cite: tad vapus tattvato jñeyaṃ vimalaṃ viśvapūraṇam | evaṃvidhe pare tattve kaḥ pūjyaḥ kaś ca tṛpyati

plain_english: Whatever state of Bhairava's is sung like this: she is the supreme one — proclaimed the supreme goddess as the supreme form.
sanskrit_cite: evaṃvidhā bhairavasya yāvasthā parigīyate | sā parā pararūpeṇa parā devī prakīrtitā

plain_english: As the non-difference of power and the powerful stands always — hence, from that property-owning, the supreme power of the supreme self.
sanskrit_cite: śaktiśaktimator yadvad abhedaḥ sarvadā sthitaḥ | atas taddharmadharmitvāt parā śaktiḥ parātmanaḥ

plain_english: No power separate from fire's burning is conceived; only in knowing-being, in entering, does this beginning arise.
sanskrit_cite: na vahner dāhikā śaktir vyatiriktā vibhāvyate | kevalaṃ jñānasattāyām prārambho 'yam praveśane

plain_english: Of one entered into the power-state, contemplation without division — then he becomes Śiva-formed: that mouth is called Śaivī.
sanskrit_cite: śaktyavasthāpraviṣṭasya nirvibhāgena bhāvanā | tadāsau śivarūpī syāt śaivī mukham ihocyate
